question: Why is it important that the sexual partners of a patient treated for an STI-related infection also get treated?

options.A: To restore normal male hormones
options.B: To prevent reinfection of the patient and stop the spread
options.C: To prevent high blood pressure in partners
options.D: To make sure the partner doesn't get a tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation: Treating partners breaks the chain of transmission. Otherwise, the patient could easily catch the infection all over again! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T31#GNS216_U5_T31_h7)

question: Why must a nurse focus on the ABCDE assessment immediately during suspected anaphylaxis instead of waiting for lab test results?

options.A: Rapid airway closure and shock can cause death within minutes
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely useless for diagnosing allergies
options.C: Skin symptoms always disappear before lab results return
options.D: Hospital protocol forbids drawing blood during emergencies

explanation: Anaphylaxis moves lightning fast. There's no time to wait for lab work when someone's airway is closing up—act first, assess fast! [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is your best first step if a painful bruise (hematoma) starts swelling up while you are trying to find a vein?

options.A: Remove the tourniquet and withdraw the needle at once
options.B: Apply an ice pack directly over the needle while it remains inside
options.C: Push the needle deeper to secure better placement in the vein
options.D: Leave the tourniquet tight and attach a larger vacuum tube

explanation: If a hematoma starts forming, stop right away! Remove the tourniquet and pull out the needle to keep the patient comfortable and prevent more bleeding under the skin. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why is it so important to involve bedside nurses when brainstorming new change ideas?

options.A: Ward managers are legally forbidden from creating improvement plans alone
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not get involved in nursing unit management
options.C: Frontline staff are the only ones who know how to use hospital computers
options.D: Frontline nurses understand the practical reality of daily ward workflows

explanation: Exactly! Bedside nurses know what really happens on the floor, which keeps our plans realistic instead of just looking good on paper. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which clinical situation requires the use of intravenous fluid therapy?

options.A: Routine daily multivitamin supplementation at home
options.B: Chronic stable hypertension controlled by diet
options.C: Severe dehydration requiring rapid fluid replacement
options.D: Mild headache treatable with swallowing pills

explanation: When fluids must be restored quickly or the gut cannot absorb them, the intravenous route is the fastest solution. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a mistake to avoid when translating IEC materials for a local community?

options.A: Translating the message into the primary local language of the community
options.B: Using clear local symbols and pictorial representations
options.C: Using literal word-for-word translation without checking local meaning
options.D: Involving local community leaders to explain key terms

explanation: Word-for-word translations can completely twist the meaning of health instructions. Always check how locals actually say it! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why is mixing minor tranquilizers with alcohol so dangerous?

options.A: Both substances slow down the nervous system and can cause breathing to stop
options.B: Alcohol chemically neutralizes the drug and causes sudden seizures
options.C: It triggers severe allergic skin rashes across the body
options.D: The combination permanently damages liver enzymes instantly

explanation: Both alcohol and minor tranquilizers are central nervous system depressants. Combined, they can dangerously shut down a person's breathing. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T4#GNS223_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and dietary supplements in Nigeria?

options.A: FMOH
options.B: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.C: WHO
options.D: NAFDAC

explanation: NAFDAC is our local body that keeps us safe by regulating drugs, food, and supplements in Nigeria. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h2)

question: What vital equipment must always be kept ready at the bedside of a patient recovering from an airway issue?

options.A: A standard blood pressure cuff and stethoscope
options.B: Suction machine and a manual breathing bag
options.C: A sterile surgical tray for major tummy surgery
options.D: An intravenous infusion pump with extra tubing

explanation: Always be prepared! Having suction and a bag-valve-mask right at the bedside lets nurses act instantly if thick mucus blocks the airway or breathing slows down. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h8)

question: During a home visit, you notice the weights for a patient's skin traction are resting on the floor. What is your very first action?

options.A: Document that the patient is non-compliant with bedrest orders
options.B: Remove the traction setup entirely because it is no longer effective
options.C: Ensure the weights hang freely without touching the floor or bed
options.D: Add extra weight to make up for the time the weights spent resting

explanation: Traction weights must always hang free! If they touch the floor, the pulling force stops, and the bones won't stay aligned. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h5)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care out in the community?

options.A: Health education, disease prevention, and personal empowerment
options.B: Performing major surgical operations in local community halls
options.C: Managing acute life-threatening trauma without medical backup
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visiting hours and meal schedules

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses focus on teaching people how to stay healthy and take charge of their own wellness. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is the urinary bladder easily injured when someone has a pelvic fracture?

options.A: Pelvic fractures cause the bladder to instantly rupture from high pressure.
options.B: The bladder is located completely outside the bony pelvis.
options.C: Fractures stop blood flow to the bladder, causing tissue death.
options.D: Sharp broken edges of the pelvic bones can puncture the bladder wall.

explanation: Think of the bladder resting right behind the pubic bone. When that bone breaks, the sharp edges can easily poke or tear the bladder next to it. Simple and logical! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h1)

question: A student nurse spots a missing decimal point on a drug order that looks way too high. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Contact the prescribing doctor to clarify the medication order before giving it
options.B: Ask another junior nurse to administer the drug since the order is official
options.C: Give the medication as written because doctors are never wrong
options.D: Administer half the dose to be safe and document the change in the chart

explanation: You are the patient's final safety net! Always pause and clarify any confusing or unsafe order with the prescriber before touching that medication cart. [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why are hospital utility bills counted as 'indirect costs'?

options.A: They are shared across the facility and cannot be tied to one patient
options.B: They are paid directly by the nursing department
options.C: They only apply to private hospital rooms
options.D: They change every single day based on the weather

explanation: Things like electricity and water keep the whole hospital running for everyone, so you can't assign them to just one single patient's bill. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for puerperal sepsis?

options.A: Rapid spontaneous vaginal birth
options.B: Early ambulation after delivery
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding
options.D: Prolonged rupture of membranes

explanation: When membranes rupture for a long time before delivery, bacteria have a direct open pathway to travel up into the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h3)

question: What is a nurse leader's best first move when handling a disagreement between community groups?

options.A: Suspend the health program until everyone calms down
options.B: Report all complaining members to the local police
options.C: Ignore the tension because arguments always resolve themselves
options.D: Listen to all sides and look for common ground

explanation: Active listening and finding shared interests help calm the tension and bring people together. You're building great leadership skills! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is visiting a patient's home so helpful for disease management?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications.
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never need a hospital visit.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe real-world habits and living conditions.
options.D: It places the entire workload on family members instead.

explanation: You get a true picture when you see where patients actually live! Home care lets you spot daily habits and environmental factors that directly affect their health. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h1)

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy can a standard medical abortion safely be done?

options.A: Up to 20 to 22 weeks
options.B: Anytime during the first trimester only
options.C: Up to 10 to 11 weeks
options.D: Strictly within the first 4 weeks

explanation: Spot on! Medical abortion is most effective and safest when used within the first 10 to 11 weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: At which tier of the IASC MHPSS pyramid are specialized psychiatric services delivered?

options.A: Tier 3
options.B: Tier 4
options.C: Tier 2
options.D: Tier 1

explanation: Spot on! Tier 4 sits right at the top of the pyramid, meant for advanced clinical care by specialists when people have severe mental health needs. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T1#GNS314_U6_T1_h1)

question: A clinic logs 95 babies for Pentavalent 1, but only 60 return for Pentavalent 3. What does this show?

options.A: A successful outreach campaign with no service delivery gaps
options.B: An excellent level of continuous retention in the immunization clinic
options.C: A high program dropout rate requiring immediate community follow-up
options.D: An oversupply of vaccines that requires immediate redistribution

explanation: Dropping from 95 down to 60 means many infants aren't completing their schedule. Time for some community tracking and follow-up! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h5)

question: Why do some families prefer having FGM done by a healthcare worker instead of a traditional cutter?

options.A: Hospitals provide free reconstructive surgery
options.B: Traditional practitioners charge higher fees
options.C: They believe clinical settings make the procedure safe
options.D: The government mandates clinical procedures

explanation: Many families think that because it's done in a clinic with clean tools and pain relief, the harmful risks disappear. But medicalised FGM is still dangerous and harmful! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: What happens when data collection for a quality project takes too much nursing time?

options.A: The government awards the hospital a special safety prize
options.B: Patients begin recording their own vital signs daily
options.C: Staff may fabricate numbers just to fill out the forms
options.D: Hospital printers automatically run out of official paper

explanation: Overly burdensome data entry leads to burnout and inaccurate reporting because bedside time is precious. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main goal of food safety in primary health care?

options.A: Disease prevention and health promotion
options.B: Regulating international food trade
options.C: Managing surgical theatre sterility
options.D: Treating advanced chronic illnesses

explanation: You've got this! Food safety at the primary health care level is all about stopping foodborne illnesses before they start and helping our communities stay healthy and strong. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h1)

question: What is a normal, mild reaction parents can expect after their baby's immunizations?

options.A: Sudden onset of severe jaundice
options.B: Slight soreness and redness at the injection site
options.C: Generalized body paralysis within two hours
options.D: Permanent hearing loss in both ears

explanation: Great work! Mild swelling or soreness is just a normal sign that the baby's body is building immunity, and it goes away on its own. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h6)

question: A patient asks why we square their height when figuring out their BMI. How should you explain it?

options.A: To adjust the weight value so it relates properly to a two-dimensional surface area
options.B: To convert the metric units into standard imperial measurements
options.C: To ensure the final number matches standard pediatric growth charts
options.D: To account for the extra weight added by heavy clothing and shoes

explanation: Well done! Squaring the height helps scale weight appropriately against body surface area rather than just a straight line measurement. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical drying side effect of anticholinergic drugs like meclizine or scopolamine?

options.A: Excessive salivation
options.B: Dry mouth
options.C: Urinary retention
options.D: Blurred vision

explanation: That's right! Anticholinergones dry things up, so you get dry mouth, not excessive drooling. Think 'can't spit, can't pee, can't see, can't stool' for anticholinergics! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h6)

question: A patient taking antibiotics for an H. pylori ulcer asks if they can stop taking the pills once the pain stops. What is the best nurse response?

options.A: Take half the remaining dose over the next few days
options.B: Stop the pills immediately to prevent drug side effects
options.C: Switch to antacids once the burning sensation stops
options.D: Complete all pills to ensure the bacteria is fully cleared

explanation: You're thinking like a true nurse! Stopping antibiotics early lets the toughest bacteria survive, leading to drug resistance and a returning ulcer. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T7#GNS213_U3_T7_h6)

question: In the Nigerian healthcare system, what is the main purpose of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: To provide specialized inpatient care for chronic diseases
options.B: To coordinate international medical research and funding
options.C: To serve as the first point of contact for health services
options.D: To handle only advanced surgical procedures and emergencies

explanation: Think of PHC as the front door of healthcare! It's the very first place individuals and families go in their community when they need health services. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why do ethics committees carefully review a study's research objectives?

options.A: To decide which nursing journal will publish the final paper
options.B: To judge if the study poses any risks to participating patients
options.C: To calculate the total financial profit of the hospital
options.D: To verify the spelling and grammar of the title page

explanation: Ethics committees check your goals to ensure that whatever you plan to study is important enough to justify any potential burden on human participants. Patient safety always comes first! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the main catch when using regular rubbing alcohol to decontaminate equipment?

options.A: It corrodes stainless steel and ruins delicate hinges
options.B: It leaves a sticky residue that attracts dirt and dust
options.C: It evaporates quickly and does not kill bacterial spores
options.D: It is completely ineffective against common viruses

explanation: Alcohol dries up fast (making it hard to keep things wet long enough) and leaves tough bacterial spores completely unfazed. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h4)

question: What two things does a Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) combine?

options.A: Both the quantity and the quality of life lived
options.B: Direct medical costs and indirect wage losses
options.C: Nurse staffing ratios and patient satisfaction ratings
options.D: Hospital operational costs and patient travel expenses

explanation: QALY looks at the bigger picture: it measures not just how long a patient lives, but how good and pain-free those years are. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which of these best describes an environmental reservoir for a disease germ?

options.A: A mosquito biting a person with malaria
options.B: An asymptomatic person carrying typhoid
options.C: A nurse caring for an infected child
options.D: Soil containing tetanus spores

explanation: Soil, water, and air can act as environmental reservoirs where germs live naturally outside of a human body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h5)

question: What are the three classic symptoms of a pheochromocytoma (an adrenal medulla tumor)?

options.A: Hypotension, hyperpigmentation, and fatigue
options.B: Headache, diaphoresis, and tachycardia
options.C: Weight gain, moon face, and purple striae
options.D: Muscle wasting, tremors, and cold intolerance

explanation: Think of a pheochromocytoma as an adrenaline factory gone wild! It triggers sudden pounding headaches, heavy sweating (diaphoresis), and a racing heart (tachycardia). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing mental health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Widespread social stigma preventing early treatment seeking
options.B: Severe shortages of trained psychiatric nurses and doctors
options.C: Inadequate government funding for healthcare infrastructure
options.D: A complete absence of mental health conditions in the population

explanation: You got it! Mental health issues are very much present in Nigeria. The real roadblocks are stigma, staff shortages, and poor funding—not a lack of illnesses. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal of dietary counselling when you're working with a patient?

options.A: Enforcing hospital cafeteria meal schedules on patients
options.B: Helping individuals make sustainable food choices for health
options.C: Strictly prescribing medications for nutritional deficiencies
options.D: Eliminating all carbohydrates from the patient daily intake

explanation: You're helping patients build lifelong healthy eating habits, not just quick fixes. Great job thinking about long-term wellness! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h1)

question: What is a major goal of skilled care when looking after someone with a long-term, chronic illness?

options.A: Elimination of all daily living assistance needs.
options.B: Complete permanent cure of the underlying disease.
options.C: Immediate discharge back to independent living.
options.D: Stabilization, symptom relief, and functional preservation.

explanation: When a chronic condition can't be cured, our goal shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, managing symptoms, and helping them stay as active as possible. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which column of spongy tissue wraps directly around the urethra inside the penis?

options.A: Corpus cavernosum
options.B: Spermatic cord
options.C: Corpus spongiosum
options.D: Tunica albuginea

explanation: The corpus spongiosum acts like a soft cushion running right along the underside, keeping the urethra open so urine and semen can pass through. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T1#GNS121_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why would a doctor prescribe corticosteroids for a patient suffering from severe serum sickness?

options.A: To replace missing complement proteins in the bloodstream
options.B: To quickly reduce widespread inflammation and immune activity
options.C: To kill any underlying bacterial infection in the skin
options.D: To permanently destroy the patient's antibody-producing cells

explanation: Corticosteroids act like a calming balm for the overactive immune system, easing the pain and swelling. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why is good nutrition during early childhood so important?

options.A: Deficits during this window can cause permanent stunting and brain damage
options.B: Young children have fully developed organs that process food slowly
options.C: It prevents the child from ever catching infections later in life
options.D: Children naturally require fewer nutrients than adults do

explanation: Think of early childhood as a critical construction phase. Missing key nutrients here can unfortunately lead to lasting effects on growth and brain development. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h1)

question: What triggers a secondary oocyte to finish its second meiotic division?

options.A: The successful entry and fusion of a sperm cell
options.B: The complete shedding of the endometrial lining
options.C: A sudden drop in systemic progesterone levels
options.D: The physical passage of the egg through the cervix

explanation: The egg stays paused in its development process until a sperm successfully enters, giving it the green light to finish dividing. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h6)

question: What is the main difference between privacy and confidentiality in research?

options.A: Privacy relates to blood samples, while confidentiality is for interviews
options.B: Privacy is a person's right to control their space, while confidentiality is our duty to protect their data
options.C: Privacy is optional, but confidentiality is required by law
options.D: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies to nurses

explanation: Spot on! Privacy belongs to the patient's personal boundaries, while confidentiality is our professional promise to keep their secrets safe. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T19#GNS224_U1_T19_h4)

question: What must a birth attendant do if a sterile item from the kit accidentally falls onto the floor?

options.A: Spray it with alcohol before using
options.B: Discard or replace the item immediately
options.C: Use it only if the floor looks dry
options.D: Wipe it clean with the kit soap and water

explanation: Once a sterile item touches the floor, its sterility is permanently compromised and it cannot be made safe for use again. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h5)

question: Which problem is most linked to using steroid eye drops for a very long time?

options.A: Severe dryness and painful ulcers
options.B: Secondary glaucoma and increased eye pressure
options.C: Rapid hardening of the outer eye layer
options.D: Permanent pupil shrinkage and total blindness

explanation: Steroids are great for short-term inflammation, but long-term use can block fluid drainage and shoot pressure right up, leading to secondary glaucoma. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: What is the biggest benefit of asking a patient to keep a sleep diary for a couple of weeks?

options.A: It permanently cures nocturnal awakenings through auto-suggestion.
options.B: It measures blood oxygen saturation levels during REM sleep.
options.C: It provides a reliable, real-time record of actual sleep patterns and habits.
options.D: It replaces the need for any nursing or medical communication.

explanation: People aren't always great at remembering how they slept. A sleep diary captures daily habits and rest patterns in real time, giving nurses accurate info to work with. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the main goal of health education in nursing?

options.A: Fulfilling mandatory legal paperwork
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment
options.C: Diagnosing complex medical conditions
options.D: Promoting health and preventing disease

explanation: Spot on! Our core job as nurses is to help people stay well and stop illnesses before they even start. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the process of changing the shape of the lens to focus on close objects called?

options.A: Accommodation
options.B: Refraction
options.C: Adaptation
options.D: Constriction

explanation: Accommodation is the eye's ability to adjust lens shape for clear near vision. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which nursing action is a great example of 'validating' a patient during an emotional crisis?

options.A: Acknowledging and accepting the reality of the patient's emotional pain
options.B: Telling the patient that their worries are completely irrational
options.C: Insisting that the patient stop crying and focus on paperwork
options.D: Changing the subject immediately to something more cheerful

explanation: Exactly. Validation means letting the patient know: 'I see your pain, I hear you, and your feelings make sense.' It builds instant trust. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h5)

question: In nursing tests and exams, what does 'validity' actually mean?

options.A: The test can be completed in under twenty minutes.
options.B: Multiple instructors will always give the exact same grade.
options.C: The test gives the exact same score every single time it is used.
options.D: The test actually measures what it is intended to measure.

explanation: A valid test is one that truly assesses the exact skill or knowledge it claims to test. No tricks—just straight to the point! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h8)

question: What happens in the body to cause an erection during sexual arousal?

options.A: Rapid dehydration of the body
options.B: Constriction of the pelvic arteries
options.C: Depletion of adrenal hormones
options.D: Vasocongestion of penile tissues

explanation: Well done! Arousal sends a rush of blood into the spongy tissues of the penis, causing them to fill up (vasocongestion) and create an erection. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h2)

question: What is the main hazard of leaving heavy oxygen cylinders unmounted inside an ambulance?

options.A: They make the ambulance engine consume more diesel fuel
options.B: They will automatically run out of medical oxygen faster
options.C: They can become dangerous projectiles during sudden braking
options.D: They interfere with the vehicle's internal electrical system

explanation: Sudden stops create massive forward momentum, turning loose heavy items into severe safety hazards for the crew and patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the main difference between a research question and a hypothesis?

options.A: A hypothesis is used only in qualitative studies
options.B: A research question is always written after data collection
options.C: A hypothesis never mentions variables or patient populations
options.D: A research question asks an inquiry, while a hypothesis makes a predicted statement

explanation: Simple rule: a research question asks a question ('Does X affect Y?'), while a hypothesis makes an educated guess at the answer ('X will increase Y'). [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h6)

question: A staff nurse administers the wrong IV fluid, injuring a patient while on duty in a public hospital. Who can be sued alongside the nurse?

options.A: The patient's next of kin
options.B: The hospital management or employing authority
options.C: The Nursing and Midwifery Council registrar
options.D: The pharmaceutical manufacturing company

explanation: Because the nurse was doing their job at the time, the hospital shares the responsibility under the rule of vicarious liability. Teamwork means shared accountability! [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h5)

question: Why is it so helpful to teach elderly patients with chronic illnesses how to monitor themselves?

options.A: It helps catch worsening symptoms early before emergency care is needed.
options.B: It eliminates all normal age-related physical decline.
options.C: It completely removes the need for regular nursing home visits.
options.D: It allows the patient to change their prescription dosages alone.

explanation: You nailed it! When patients keep an eye on their own warning signs, little issues get caught early—long before they turn into scary hospital emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h3)

question: When is an asynchronous tele-nursing approach most useful?

options.A: When conducting a cardiac resuscitation emergency call
options.B: When sending recorded data or messages for a nurse to review later
options.C: When a patient is actively bleeding and needs immediate instructions
options.D: When performing a live physical examination over video

explanation: Think of asynchronous care as 'store-and-forward.' The patient sends a message or reading, and you check it when you have a moment. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why does ongoing urinary incontinence put a patient at higher risk for urinary tract infections?

options.A: Skin breakdown allows bacteria to travel directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Frequent urination washes away all the normal protective cells
options.C: Moisture and residual urine create an environment where bacteria multiply easily
options.D: Absorbent pads permanently stop the kidneys from filtering waste

explanation: Sticking around in lingering moisture gives bacteria a cozy place to grow and easily find their way into the urinary tract. Good skin care and hygiene prevent this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of adaptive equipment in rehabilitation?

options.A: To help clients perform daily tasks independently despite physical limits
options.B: To monitor the daily vital signs of clients living at home
options.C: To speed up the biological knitting of broken bone fragments
options.D: To completely replace the need for physical therapy and exercise

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive tools give patients clever ways to wash, dress, and eat on their own without always needing help. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h7)

question: What is the main reason for evaluating an outbreak after it has ended?

options.A: To learn from response strengths and weaknesses to improve future preparedness
options.B: To increase taxes on communities that experienced high infection rates
options.C: To punish health workers who made mistakes during the emergency peak
options.D: To permanently close down the healthcare facilities that treated patients

explanation: Post-outbreak reviews help our health systems learn what went right and what to fix before the next emergency hits. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h8)

question: What usually happens to ordinary families when they have to pay heavy out-of-pocket costs for healthcare?

options.A: Guaranteed reimbursement of medical bills by local governments
options.B: Catastrophic health expenditures that drain household savings
options.C: Automatic enrollment in free federal health insurance schemes
options.D: Immediate access to advanced surgical care in private hospitals

explanation: When you have to pay straight from your pocket without insurance, sudden illnesses can easily wipe out a family's savings and drag them into severe poverty. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h1)

question: When doing a 24-hour dietary recall, what does the nurse ask the client to do?

options.A: List everything they ate over the past 24 hours
options.B: Predict their exact food budget for the coming year
options.C: Fast for a full day before visiting the clinic
options.D: Cook a demonstration meal for the nursing staff

explanation: Easy peasy! A 24-hour dietary recall is simply asking the client to list everything they ate and drank recently. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h2)

question: Which healthcare professional primarily helps a child with cerebral palsy learn how to perform daily living tasks like eating and dressing independently?

options.A: Respiratory therapist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Speech pathologist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists specialize in helping patients develop fine motor skills needed for everyday activities and self-care. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h6)

question: A patient comes back two days after an abscess drainage with a fever and redness that is spreading outward from the wound. What does this mean?

options.A: Worsening infection requiring prompt medical reassessment
options.B: An allergic reaction to the cotton inside the dressing
options.C: Successful eradication of all bacteria from the body
options.D: Normal healing response as the deep tissues close

explanation: Spreading redness and fever are warning signs that the infection is fighting back and traveling further. The patient needs a doctor to take a look right away. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which scenario is an example of natural passive immunity?

options.A: A patient recovering completely from a severe bout of malaria
options.B: A pregnant woman receiving a tetanus toxoid booster shot
options.C: An infant receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.D: A traveler receiving a shot of hepatitis B immunoglobulin

explanation: Passing antibodies from a mother to her baby via breast milk or the placenta is a natural way to provide temporary passive protection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why are finger foods so helpful for patients with advanced dementia during meals?

options.A: It prevents the patient from spilling liquids on their hospital gown
options.B: It guarantees the patient will eat three full meals every single day
options.C: It promotes independence and makes eating easier for confused patients
options.D: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff supervision

explanation: Spot on! When handling cutlery gets confusing, finger foods let patients feed themselves and hold onto their dignity. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T3#GNS212_U1_T3_h5)

question: What do we call the emotional tiredness and burnout nurses feel from caring for suffering patients day after day?

options.A: Perceived loss
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Complex mourning
options.D: Compassion fatigue

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when we absorb so much patient trauma and stress without taking time to recharge ourselves. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h8)

question: Why are the spaces (sutures) between the baby's skull bones so important during labour?

options.A: They lock the head in a fixed position to stop accidental rotation.
options.B: They supply oxygen directly to the developing foetal brain tissue.
options.C: They prevent any fluid from entering the cranial vault during birth.
options.D: They allow the skull bones to overlap and reduce the head size.

explanation: Those little gaps act like expansion joints! They let the skull bones slide over each other slightly, making the head a bit smaller so it can fit smoothly through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h2)

question: When should standard infection control precautions be applied in a reproductive health clinic?

options.A: Exclusively during surgical childbirth procedures
options.B: Only when visitors are observing the clinical ward
options.C: To every single client regardless of infection status
options.D: Only when caring for patients with confirmed infections

explanation: Correct! Treat every patient's body fluids as potentially infectious. This keeps both you and the patients safe every single day. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of food distribution systems?

options.A: Setting international trade tariffs on crops
options.B: Regulating chemical use in commercial farming
options.C: Moving food from farms to consumers
options.D: Determining the retail price of imported meat

explanation: Food distribution is fundamentally about bridging the physical gap between agricultural production sites and the final consumer. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h1)

question: How do vital signs usually change when a patient has severe fluid loss (hypovolemia)?

options.A: Heart rate increases and blood pressure drops
options.B: Both heart rate and blood pressure drop significantly
options.C: Both heart rate and blood pressure increase
options.D: Heart rate drops and blood pressure rises

explanation: Spot on! With less fluid in the pipes, blood pressure falls, and the heart races to try and keep circulation moving. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h6)

question: Where can healthcare workers quickly find safety details, hazard warnings, and emergency steps for a specific chemical?

options.A: Hospital dietary meal manual
options.B: Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
options.C: General nursing care textbook
options.D: Daily facility staffing schedule

explanation: Every hospital department has them. The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is your best friend for looking up how to safely handle a chemical and what to do if an accident happens. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h8)

question: A patient notices her resting body temperature goes up slightly during the second half of her cycle. Which hormone causes this shift?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: FSH
options.C: Estriol
options.D: GnRH

explanation: Progesterone is thermogenic, meaning it naturally bumps up basal body temperature slightly right after ovulation. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of pressure redistribution for patients who spend all day in bed?

options.A: Accelerating the breakdown of red blood cells
options.B: Increasing the overall room temperature
options.C: Spreading body weight to protect delicate skin
options.D: Making it easier to change hospital pajamas

explanation: That's correct! Spreading weight across a larger surface area takes the harsh, concentrated pressure off bony areas, helping to keep the skin safe and healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why must a patient rinse their mouth with water after using a steroid inhaler?

options.A: To wash away any bitter taste left behind on the tongue
options.B: To prevent the development of oral fungal infections like thrush
options.C: To stimulate saliva production for better lung absorption
options.D: To cool down the throat after the cold propellant spray

explanation: Steroids left behind in the mouth can lower local immunity and cause a fungal infection called thrush. A simple rinse and spit is all it takes to prevent this! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h3)

question: What is the primary direction of time in a prospective research design?

options.A: Moving backward from the present into the past
options.B: Comparing two different time periods in history
options.C: Moving forward from the present into the future
options.D: Examining past medical records for current outcomes

explanation: Prospective studies are designed to follow participants forward in time to observe future outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why do uterine contractions eventually become weaker during a prolonged, blocked labour?

options.A: The uterine muscle runs out of energy from overworking
options.B: The maternal kidneys start retaining excess fluids
options.C: The placenta stops producing progesterone
options.D: The baby's heartbeat suppresses uterine activity

explanation: Think of the uterus like any other muscle in the body. If it keeps pushing hard against a blockage without a break, it eventually gets exhausted and runs out of energy! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: Which neurological condition can be managed using anticholinergics to help reduce tremors?

options.A: Epilepsy
options.B: Multiple sclerosis
options.C: Alzheimer's disease
options.D: Parkinson's disease

explanation: Anticholinergics help balance neurotransmitters in the brain to control tremors in early Parkinson's disease. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is a very common cause of esophageal strictures (narrowing) that need dilation?

options.A: Chronic acid reflux disease
options.B: Benign gastric hypersecretion
options.C: Excessive dietary fiber intake
options.D: Congenital throat widening

explanation: When stomach acid keeps splashing up into the esophagus over a long time, it irritates the tissue, causes scarring, and makes the passage narrow. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h3)

question: Which of these is a safe and secure computer habit for clinical staff?

options.A: Sharing personal login passwords with trusted colleagues
options.B: Writing computer access codes on public office sticky notes
options.C: Leaving patient medical records open on unattended screens
options.D: Logging out of the computer workstation when leaving the desk

explanation: Always locking your screen or logging out keeps patient data safe from prying eyes when you step away. Great habit to build early! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is a modern, digital way to share nursing research?

options.A: Paper memos locked inside a supervisor desk drawer
options.B: Locked institutional archives in university basements
options.C: Professional social media networks and infographics
options.D: Printed textbooks published twenty years ago

explanation: Exactly! Digital tools like social media and colorful infographics help spread useful health tips quickly to a wide audience. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient walks with an unsteady gait and cannot easily touch their finger to their nose. Which area is likely affected?

options.A: Medulla oblongata
options.B: Occipital lobe
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: When balance and smooth coordination are off during physical tests, it points straight to the cerebellum. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of bowel preparation before rectovaginal fistula surgery?

options.A: To reduce fecal load and minimize infection risk
options.B: To increase blood pressure during the operation
options.C: To stretch the vaginal walls for easier access
options.D: To test the kidneys for dye clearance

explanation: Clearing the bowel reduces stool contamination at the surgical site, lowering the risk of postoperative wound infection and failure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: Which service is typically included as a core offering in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Complex intravenous chemotherapy administration
options.B: Intensive care unit mechanical ventilation
options.C: Major orthopedic surgical procedures
options.D: Assistance with daily personal hygiene and bathing

explanation: Personal care assistance with hygiene, dressing, and bathing forms the core foundation of daily services in assisted living. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h3)

question: What happens first during the assessment phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Evaluating whether the patient has achieved their health goals
options.B: Writing the final medical diagnosis for the patient's chart
options.C: Collecting subjective and objective data about the patient's health status
options.D: Administering prescribed medications and performing wound care procedures

explanation: Assessment is always step one! It's like being a detective—gathering clues by talking to the patient, doing a physical check, and looking at lab results. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which hardworking hormone tells the kidneys to hold onto sodium and water while letting go of potassium?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Aldosterone is your kidney's best friend for saving water and sodium when your body needs to boost its volume. You're crushing it! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h4)

question: What happens to extra glucose when your body already has enough energy?

options.A: It is stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen
options.B: It is turned into red blood cells in the spleen
options.C: It is immediately converted into bone marrow cells
options.D: It is excreted entirely through the sweat glands

explanation: When there's extra sugar around, the body packs it neatly away in the liver and muscles as glycogen for later use. Smart storage! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h4)

question: How does severe protein-energy malnutrition directly weaken a person's immune system?

options.A: By depriving the body of building blocks needed to make immune cells and antibodies
options.B: By stopping the liver from producing digestive enzymes
options.C: By destroying red blood cells in the spleen
options.D: By increasing blood pressure too quickly for white cells to circulate

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Just like you need blocks to build a house, your body needs protein to build antibodies and white blood cells. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h4)

question: A patient experiences severe dehydration. What immediate effect does this have on body function?

options.A: Sudden increase in muscle mass and bone density
options.B: Immediate conversion of fats into stored carbohydrates
options.C: Disruption of metabolic processes and electrolyte balance
options.D: Rapid overproduction of digestive enzymes in the gut

explanation: Without enough water, blood volume drops, electrolytes concentrate abnormally, and cellular chemical reactions slow down or fail. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h4)

question: What does a realistic healthcare plan take into account?

options.A: The personal hobbies of the hospital director
options.B: Architectural designs from foreign hospitals
options.C: International travel trends for medical tourists
options.D: Current staffing levels and available budget

explanation: A realistic plan matches its ambitions to what the facility can actually afford and staff right now. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is teaching job skills (vocational training) so helpful in rehab programs for recovering users?

options.A: It replaces the need for any prescription medications during detox
options.B: It guarantees they will pass all school board examinations
options.C: It equips them with economic skills to rebuild their lives after treatment
options.D: It legally prevents them from ever feeling stressed again

explanation: Giving recovering individuals a way to make an honest living helps prevent poverty and unemployment, which often cause relapse. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h9)

question: How does your skin play a vital role in keeping your bones strong with calcium?

options.A: By filtering calcium out through the sebaceous glands
options.B: By synthesizing vitamin D precursors using UV light
options.C: By storing dietary calcium directly in the epidermis
options.D: By producing specialized calcium-binding sweat

explanation: Fantastic! Sunlight hits the skin to jumpstart vitamin D production, which your gut needs to absorb calcium properly. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is meant by a disease 'reservoir'?

options.A: Where the infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The Department of Health data storage unit
options.C: A device used to measure patient body temperature
options.D: The specific medication given to kill a virus

explanation: Correct! A reservoir is the natural hiding and breeding place—whether in humans, animals, or soil—where a germ thrives and reproduces. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h3)

question: Why might a traumatized patient complain of chest tightness and nausea even when all their medical tests are normal?

options.A: The patient is intentionally trying to fake their injuries
options.B: A delayed infection is spreading through the bloodstream
options.C: Somatization translates emotional stress into physical symptoms
options.D: Standard hospital diagnostic machines are malfunctioning

explanation: Exactly! The mind and body are deeply connected. Emotional distress can show up as very real physical feelings like upset stomachs or tight chests—this is called somatization. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h2)

question: Why might two different people with the same medical condition react completely differently?

options.A: Doctors always prescribe different treatments for identical diseases
options.B: Disease is purely subjective while illness is objective
options.C: Illness is the personal experience and interpretation of symptoms
options.D: Physical pathology dictates every single action a person takes

explanation: Disease is what the body has, but illness is how the person feels and experiences it. Everyone's perspective is unique! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T9#GNS123_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which of these best describes for-profit healthcare providers?

options.A: They are strictly owned and managed by local government councils
options.B: They operate as commercial businesses aiming to generate financial returns
options.C: They offer free medical services to every member of the public
options.D: They rely exclusively on volunteer staff and donated medical supplies

explanation: Correct! For-profit clinics run like businesses, meaning making a financial return is part of keeping their doors open. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h4)

question: Why is careful pin-site care so important for a patient with an external fixator?

options.A: To encourage faster bone mineralization around the pin insertion sites
options.B: To prevent bacteria from traveling down the metal pins into the bone
options.C: To stop the external metal frame from rusting over time
options.D: To prevent the skin from sticking permanently to the metal frame

explanation: Since the pins go through the skin, they create a pathway for germs. Keeping them clean stops nasty deep bone infections like osteomyelitis! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the community health planning cycle?

options.A: To replace traditional healers with orthodox medical practitioners
options.B: To punish communities that fail to follow sanitation guidelines
options.C: To systematically address population health problems using available resources
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in tertiary hospitals

explanation: The planning cycle provides a structured framework for public health nurses to tackle community-wide health issues efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the main drawback of using a quick survey (cross-sectional study) to prove cause and effect?

options.A: Cross-sectional surveys only capture data at one single point in time
options.B: Surveys are always illegal to conduct inside modern hospitals
options.C: Statistical software cannot process survey data
options.D: Participants never answer survey questions honestly

explanation: You got it! Because a survey takes a snapshot at just one moment, you can't tell which came first—the cause or the effect. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h7)

question: If you don't have a tissue handy and suddenly need to cough, what should you do?

options.A: Cough into your inner elbow
options.B: Cough directly into the open air
options.C: Turn your head toward the nearest wall
options.D: Cover your mouth with both bare hands

explanation: Brilliant! Coughing into your elbow keeps the droplets off your hands. If you cough into your hands, you'll just transfer those germs to every door handle and chart you touch! [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h5)

question: A mother cannot afford the expensive imported supplements recommended for her underweight toddler. As her nurse, what should you do?

options.A: Tell her that nutrition counseling is no longer necessary if she cannot afford items
options.B: Help the mother adapt affordable, locally available foods to enrich the child's diet
options.C: Advise her to stop feeding the child solid foods until financial aid arrives
options.D: Insist that she buy the expensive supplements regardless of her financial situation

explanation: Real nursing meets people where they are. Great health education uses accessible, local market foods to make nutritious meals practical for every family. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h7)

question: How does organizing the partograph into specific sections help you as a busy nurse?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to ever take manual blood pressure
options.B: It reduces the total duration of the first stage of labour by half
options.C: It ensures systematic and organized data collection without missing vital signs
options.D: It allows family members to fill out the medical chart independently

explanation: Having dedicated sections keeps your charting neat and ensures you never forget a vital check for either the mother or her baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h2)

question: How should an airport security check be handled for a passenger with a pacemaker?

options.A: Turn off the pacemaker completely using an external switch before entering the security line
options.B: Walk through the metal detector normally, but ask security to avoid using a hand-held wand over the chest
options.C: Show the medical card and demand a full body cavity search instead of walking through arches
options.D: Refuse all security screening because airport machines will instantly destroy the pacemaker

explanation: Walking through the security arch is usually fine if you keep moving, but security should avoid holding a magnetic wand directly over the chest. Practical knowledge for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why does the electrical signal take a short pause at the AV node?

options.A: To stop signals from going backward into the lungs
options.B: To slow down the heart rate during sleep
options.C: To give the SA node time to rest
options.D: To let the ventricles fill up completely with blood first

explanation: That tiny pause is super smart design! It ensures the top chambers finish emptying their blood down into the bottom chambers before the bottom chambers squeeze. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: How do many individuals with behaviour disorders view neutral, everyday actions from other people?

options.A: As deliberate threats
options.B: As acts of confusion
options.C: As friendly gestures
options.D: As signs of weakness

explanation: They often have a 'hostile attribution bias,' meaning they wrongly assume others are out to get them even when they aren't. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is low immunization coverage in a community dangerous?

options.A: It increases the risk of vaccine-preventable disease outbreaks
options.B: It reduces the overall population growth rate
options.C: It causes immediate financial inflation in local markets
options.D: It automatically lowers the literacy rate among children

explanation: Spot on! When too few people are vaccinated, herd immunity drops, making it easy for dangerous infections to spread among vulnerable ones. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h1)

question: Which statement best describes the role of nurse managers when using scheduling software?

options.A: They have no control over the roster once the computer generates it
options.B: They are only responsible for entering patient billing data into the system
options.C: They stop working night shifts completely because software handles them
options.D: They must still review and adjust schedules for human factors and emergencies

explanation: Software assists with the math, but nurse managers must use clinical judgment for unexpected personal situations. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why is knowing the exact date of a patient's last menstrual period (LMP) so important?

options.A: It proves the patient has reached full menopause
options.B: It establishes a baseline for dating a pregnancy or spotting cycle changes
options.C: It indicates the exact day ovulation will occur next month
options.D: It measures the total amount of iron stored in the blood

explanation: You will use this all the time in clinic! The LMP helps us calculate expected due dates for pregnant mums and spot any unusual bleeding patterns early. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which of these best describes probability sampling?

options.A: Participants are chosen simply because they are easy to find and talk to
options.B: The researcher hand-picks participants who agree with their hypothesis
options.C: Every member of the population has a known chance of being selected
options.D: Only patients with severe symptoms are allowed to join the study

explanation: Awesome! Probability sampling uses fairness and randomization, meaning nobody is unfairly favored and everyone has an equal shot at being picked. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h4)

question: What trouble can happen if nurse managers focus too much on economic efficiency?

options.A: It automatically lowers the salary of all registered nurses on the unit
options.B: It makes patient vital sign monitoring completely unnecessary
options.C: It can conflict with the ethical duty to provide equitable care to all patients
options.D: It forces physicians to perform surgeries without any nursing assistance

explanation: If we only chase the cheapest options to save money, vulnerable patients who need expensive care might get left behind. Nursing is about fairness, not just profit! [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h7)

question: How can nurses best help prevent FGM within local communities?

options.A: By educating families and working with local leaders to change attitudes
options.B: By reporting every pregnant woman to international human rights courts
options.C: By offering safe, clean clinical alternatives for young girls
options.D: By focusing only on treating women who already have complications

explanation: Prevention relies on grassroots education and community engagement to address the root cultural drivers of FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What does a very small standard deviation mean for a set of patient temperature readings?

options.A: The readings are closely clustered near the average temperature
options.B: The highest temperature reading was far above normal limits
options.C: There was a major calculation error made during data entry
options.D: The patients have completely different underlying health conditions

explanation: A small standard deviation means everyone's readings are hugging close to the average—very little variation! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T5#GNS217_U4_T5_h3)

question: What does a "double burden of disease" mean in Nigerian public health?

options.A: Having high rates of both maternal and child mortality simultaneously
options.B: Suffering from simultaneous outbreaks of waterborne and airborne infections
options.C: Managing high patient loads in both rural clinics and urban teaching hospitals
options.D: Dealing with both infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases

explanation: Great job! A double burden simply means our healthcare system has to fight old enemies like malaria and TB while also managing the rising wave of lifestyle diseases like hypertension and diabetes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is a common complication when anxiety disorders are left untreated for many years?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to speak
options.B: Development of co-occurring depression and substance abuse
options.C: Complete immunity to all forms of psychological stress
options.D: Spontaneous cure of all medical health problems

explanation: Carrying heavy, unmanaged anxiety wears down a person's emotional strength over time, often opening the door to depression or unhealthy coping habits. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h8)

question: How does bovine mastitis (udder infection) directly affect raw milk?

options.A: It forces the cow to stop producing any milk permanently
options.B: It introduces pathogenic bacteria directly into the milk stream
options.C: It completely sterilizes the milk inside the udder gland
options.D: It increases the acid level enough to kill all other germs

explanation: Exactly! Mastitis means the cow's udder is infected, which unfortunately dumps disease-causing germs right into the milk as it's being produced. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h2)

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle do you actually carry out your new idea on a small scale?

options.A: Do phase
options.B: Act phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Plan phase

explanation: The 'Do' phase is where the action happens! You test your idea on the ward and see how it works in real life. [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h3)

question: An asthmatic patient starts wheezing and coughing after spending the afternoon outside on a heavy smog day. What caused this attack?

options.A: Inflammation and bronchoconstriction caused by inhaled air pollutants
options.B: An allergic reaction to pollen-free chemical gases
options.C: A sudden bacterial invasion of the bloodstream
options.D: Complete destruction of the heart valves due to low oxygen

explanation: Correct! Smog irritates sensitive airways, making the muscles around them tighten up and swell, which triggers asthma symptoms. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following is a major barrier to safe motherhood in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of fully equipped emergency hospitals
options.B: Too many skilled midwives working in remote villages
options.C: Free transportation services for all pregnant women
options.D: Inadequate health infrastructure and out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Poor facilities and the burden of paying out-of-pocket for treatment prevent many Nigerian women from getting timely care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: What position should your patient be in when they drink fluids to prevent choking?

options.A: Upright at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Flat on their back in bed
options.C: Propped up at a 15-degree angle
options.D: Lying entirely on their left side

explanation: Gravity is your friend! Sitting upright helps guide liquids safely down the food pipe instead of heading toward the airway. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h6)

question: What is a major economic consequence of rising fuel prices on the food supply chain?

options.A: Immediate elimination of all post-harvest crop losses
options.B: Increased transport costs leading to higher market prices
options.C: Mandatory freezing of wholesale food prices by the government
options.D: Instant reduction in the total number of farming families

explanation: Because food must be hauled long distances, higher fuel costs directly inflate the final retail price paid by consumers. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h5)

question: What attitude is most essential for a nurse when assessing a patient with a history of FGM?

options.A: Paternalistic and authoritative
options.B: Skeptical and questioning
options.C: Non-judgmental and culturally sensitive
options.D: Indifferent and strictly clinical

explanation: Patients require a safe, empathetic environment free from moral judgment to discuss sensitive genital trauma openly. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of these shows direct clinical competence during a nurse's evaluation?

options.A: The total number of personal phone calls made on duty
options.B: How well the nurse gets along with the hospital director
options.C: Correct medication administration technique
options.D: Whether the nurse wears fashionable shoes to work

explanation: Clinical competence is all about the actual nursing care you give. Getting your drug calculations and administration spot-on is a classic example! [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h2)

question: What does CPOE stand for in health informatics?

options.A: Computerized Provider Order Entry
options.B: Certified Practical Nursing Operation
options.C: Clinical Patient Online Evaluation
options.D: Centralized Pharmacy Order Equipment

explanation: CPOE is the electronic system clinicians use to input medical orders directly, replacing messy handwritten prescriptions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of these statements about informed consent in qualitative interviews is FALSE?

options.A: It ensures participants know what the study is about
options.B: It protects the voluntary nature of participation
options.C: It only matters before the interview starts and is then forgotten
options.D: It is a continuous process that can be withdrawn at any time

explanation: You got it! Consent isn't just a paper signed at the beginning—a patient can change their mind and step out of the study at any point. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h6)

question: Why is a nurse's voice so important when planning healthcare in places with limited resources?

options.A: Nurses decide which pharmaceutical companies win government contracts
options.B: Nurses hold the highest political office in health ministries
options.C: Nurses understand practical frontline needs and realistic interventions
options.D: Nurses are solely responsible for funding hospital budgets

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses work side-by-side with patients every single day, they know what actually works on the ground. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h1)

question: How does a 'just culture' help a hospital reduce unwanted variation in care?

options.A: By punishing anyone who deviates from standard hospital routine
options.B: By ensuring every nurse receives the exact same annual salary bonus
options.C: By removing all nursing supervisors from clinical hospital wards
options.D: By encouraging staff to report workflow issues and near-misses safely

explanation: You're a star! A just culture builds trust so nurses feel safe speaking up about problems before anyone gets hurt. Keep up the awesome work! [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which action must happen BEFORE the ambulance begins moving with a trauma victim?

options.A: Washing the inside of the transport vehicle thoroughly
options.B: Securing the airway and controlling major external bleeding
options.C: Completing a full neurological surgery consultation
options.D: Discharging the patient's family members from the scene

explanation: Life-threatening issues involving breathing and circulation must be addressed on the scene before the vehicle starts moving. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h2)

question: In the famous 'Three Delays' model, what is the first delay all about?

options.A: The wait time to see a doctor at the hospital
options.B: The time spent traveling on bad rural roads
options.C: The decision by the family to seek medical help
options.D: The delay in manufacturing lifesaving drugs

explanation: Exactly right! The first delay happens right at home when family members take too long to recognize danger signs or decide it's time to visit a clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h5)

question: Why is a previous cesarean section considered a contraindication for home delivery?

options.A: Community nurses do not know how to care for scars
options.B: Stitches from the old scar will itch
options.C: Risk of uterine rupture during labor
options.D: The baby will always be too large

explanation: A scarred uterus can tear open under the pressure of contractions, which is a life-threatening emergency requiring a surgical suite. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why should families pick a specific meeting place outside their home when planning for emergencies?

options.A: To ensure everyone can reunite safely if separated during an evacuation
options.B: To provide a storage space for heavy rescue tools
options.C: To serve as a temporary community clinic
options.D: To give neighbors a place to park their vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Having a pre-arranged meeting spot saves precious time and stops panic if family members get separated during a sudden crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why don't modern hospitals just use simple boiling water to process surgical instruments?

options.A: It leaves a toxic chemical residue on the metal surface
options.B: It melts stainless steel components and plastic handles
options.C: It fails to reliably destroy bacterial endospores
options.D: It takes significantly longer than standard steam autoclaves

explanation: Boiling water is great for killing regular bacteria, but some hardy spores can survive 100°C. That's why we rely on autoclaves instead! [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is a major ethical puzzle that community health nurses face more often than hospital nurses?

options.A: Managing hospital bed capacity during unexpected equipment shortages
options.B: Choosing whether to discharge a patient before lab results are printed
options.C: Balancing individual personal autonomy with the safety of the wider public
options.D: Deciding which doctor receives a larger salary bonus at the end of the month

explanation: You've got it! Community nurses constantly balance respecting a person's individual choices with protecting the whole public from health risks like infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h5)

question: A nurse sorts patients by their blood groups (A, B, AB, or O). What level of measurement is this?

options.A: Ratio
options.B: Ordinal
options.C: Nominal
options.D: Interval

explanation: Spot on! Blood groups are just names or categories with no numerical value or rank. Whenever you're just labeling categories, it's nominal data. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h2)

question: What happens when DRF drugs are sold way below their replacement cost?

options.A: Higher wages for the hospital dispensing personnel
options.B: Faster delivery of goods from pharmaceutical suppliers
options.C: Increased trust from the community healthcare board
options.D: Depletion of capital and eventual stockouts

explanation: If you sell something for 100 naira but it costs 150 naira to replace it, your fund shrinks a little bit every time. Eventually, your shelves will be totally bare! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks when assessing a patient's personal host status?

options.A: Screening for underlying chronic illnesses like diabetes
options.B: Inquiring about recent travel history to endemic regions
options.C: Reviewing the patient's personal immunization records
options.D: Analyzing the genetic makeup of the local water supply

explanation: Host assessment is all about the *person* sitting in front of you—their health, vaccines, and history. Water genetics belong to environmental health, not individual patient assessment! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h6)

question: Where is the substantia nigra physically located in the central nervous system?

options.A: At the base of the spinal cord
options.B: Within the midbrain
options.C: Inside the cerebral cortex
options.D: Directly inside the lateral ventricles

explanation: The substantia nigra is a dark-pigmented nucleus located in the midbrain that produces dopamine for the basal ganglia circuits. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why is community participation critical after a health plan has been created?

options.A: It prevents the local government from taxing the primary health center
options.B: It creates a sense of ownership so the community maintains the project
options.C: It ensures that health workers receive extra allowances from donors
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all their daily workload to local volunteers

explanation: When communities participate in identifying and planning solutions, they protect and sustain the project long after external funding ends. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do private healthcare facilities tend to avoid opening branches in poor rural communities?

options.A: Governments forbid private clinics in rural zones
options.B: The expected financial return is too low
options.C: Rural residents never experience health problems
options.D: Staff refuse to live outside major cities

explanation: Profit-driven enterprises invest where patients have the financial means to pay for services, leading to rural medical deserts. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is an anticholinergic drug like atropine given along with neostigmine?

options.A: To make the reversal agent work twice as fast in an emergency
options.B: To keep the patient deeply asleep while the breathing tube is removed
options.C: To prevent dangerous spikes in blood pressure caused by neostigmine
options.D: To counteract unwanted slow heart rate and increased secretions caused by neostigmine

explanation: Neostigmine can cause bradycardia and too much spit or mucus. Atropine steps in to dry things up and keep the heart rate steady! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the main reason nurses use portable monitors in the hospital?

options.A: To track vital signs while a patient is moving
options.B: To permanently store a patient's entire medical history
options.C: To deliver intravenous medications automatically
options.D: To replace all stationary equipment in the intensive care unit

explanation: Portable monitors are lifesavers when patients are walking around or being moved between wards. They let us keep a close eye on vitals on the go! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h1)

question: How is pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) affecting the Fallopian tubes primarily treated in a stable patient?

options.A: Continuous peritoneal dialysis
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Immediate emergency surgery
options.D: Radiation therapy

explanation: You're crushing it. Because PID is an infection, the frontline treatment is medical—hitting it hard with the right antibiotics to clear the bacteria. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h5)

question: You walk into a ward and see that your patient's traction weights are resting on the floor. What is your very next move?

options.A: Lift the weights and ensure they hang freely
options.B: Remove the traction apparatus immediately
options.C: Add more weight to make up for lost time
options.D: Document that the therapy is finished

explanation: Quick thinking! Just lift them up so they hang free again, and traction is instantly restored. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h4)

question: Which of these is a great example of community-level disaster prep?

options.A: Clearing blocked drainage channels together before the rainy season begins
options.B: Relying entirely on federal radio broadcasts for weather updates
options.C: Waiting inside a flooded home for international rescue helicopters
options.D: Reporting abandoned buildings only after they collapse

explanation: Brilliant! Clearing drains together is a practical grassroots action that stops floods before the heavy rains even start. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do qualitative researchers usually find key insights in interview texts?

options.A: By searching for recurring themes and patterns in text transcripts
options.B: By calculating the mean and standard deviation of blood tests
options.C: By running computer programs that solve complex algebra equations
options.D: By measuring the exact dosage of medication given to patients

explanation: Instead of crunching numbers, qualitative researchers read carefully through transcripts to find common themes and powerful quotes. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h5)

question: Which of these is a dangerous medication habit that you should warn patients against?

options.A: Checking expiration dates on packaging before swallowing pills
options.B: Reporting any unusual itching or rashes to your healthcare provider
options.C: Sharing your leftover antibiotics with sick family members
options.D: Completing the entire dose prescribed by a qualified doctor

explanation: Never share your drugs! Dosage needs vary from person to person, and what cures your infection could harm someone else. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of these common STIs is caused by bacteria and can be easily cured with antibiotics?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.C: Chlamydia
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Great job! Chlamydia is bacterial, which means standard antibiotics clear it right up. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: How do accidental and intentional poisonings usually look different when patients arrive?

options.A: Accidental cases frequently involve children and single agents, while intentional cases often involve adults and multiple drugs
options.B: Intentional poisonings are completely untreatable compared to accidental exposures
options.C: Intentional poisonings only occur through inhalation, whereas accidental poisonings always involve swallowing
options.D: Accidental exposures never require medical attention, unlike all intentional exposures

explanation: Spot on! Little ones often accidentally swallow just one household item, whereas intentional adult cases more often involve multiple medications. Knowing this helps you prepare for what to expect! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h1)

question: A researcher notices many patients stopped attending a 6-month weight loss study before it ended. What is this called?

options.A: The Hawthorne effect
options.B: A confounding variable
options.C: Attrition bias
options.D: Random assignment

explanation: You nailed it! 'Attrition' just means people dropping out over time, which can leave us with a lopsided group of results. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T2#GNS217_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is it risky to just sit back and trust bedside monitors blindly?

options.A: Bedside machines drain too much electricity from the room
options.B: Monitors can show false readings or artifact that require physical verification
options.C: Monitors are generally illegal to use without a physician present
options.D: Monitors only measure body temperature and nothing else

explanation: Machines are great helpers, but they aren't human! A simple movement can mess up the reading. Always double-check the monitor numbers by actually looking at and touching your patient. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h2)

question: A nursing student accidentally pokes themselves with a needle used on a patient with Hepatitis B. What immediate action should be taken?

options.A: Advising the worker to stay home from work for exactly two weeks
options.B: Administering Hepatitis B immune globulin and starting the vaccine series if unvaccinated
